result:
`src/slug.js` is fixed — the regex replace was leaving stray leading/trailing hyphens (e.g. `"  Hello, World!  "` → `-hello-world-` instead of `hello-world`). I added a trim step to strip leading/trailing hyphens after the punctuation collapse:

```js
return title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
```

I did not touch `test/slug.test.js`. Running the test file directly with Node's test runner, all 4 assertions pass:

```
node --test test/slug.test.js
# tests 4, pass 4, fail 0
```

One thing worth flagging: in this sandboxed shell, the literal `npm test` command (which runs `node --test test/`) errors out with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — Node seems to be treating the bare `test/` directory argument as a script to `require()` rather than scanning it for test files. This reproduces with plain `node --test test/` too, but *not* with `node --test` (no args, default cwd scan) or `node --test test/*.test.js`/`test/slug.test.js` explicitly — both of those find and pass all 4 tests. This looks like an artifact of this particular sandbox rather than something wrong with your code or test files, so I left `package.json` alone rather than guessing at a workaround you didn't ask for. If `npm test` also fails this way in your actual environment, let me know and I can look at the test script invocation.
